pr_title: drivers: video: Conversion of k_work API
pr_body:
Replace deprecated API with the recommended alternative.

Fixes: #34090
Signed-off-by: Loic Poulain <loic.poulain@linaro.org>
pr_comments:
> This is OK from the perspective of changing the API.
> 
> The race conditions in the driver are unchanged: issuing an unchecked work cancel does not eliminate the data race between the work handler and other threads accessing the generator data.

I've replaced cancel with cancel_sync to ensure it is not running once stopped (until it is restarted). Not sure about what race you're pointing here, the work mostly play with fifo_get/put which is AFAIK thread safe. Other elements like video data pattern are not 'changed' while the video stream (and so the work) is running (started).

issue_context.title: Convert video_sw_generator.c to new kwork API
issue_context.body:
Convert drivers/video/video_sw_generator.c to use new kwork API.

See the following issue for details:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/33104

review_comments: ~Changing to `_sync` doesn't solve the problem: a cancel can fail, and if it does you have a race condition.~
Re-reading my own documentation: that's not true; the work item will be idle when this completes.  Note that `stop()` can no longer be invoked from an ISR, though.

> Re-reading my own documentation: that's not true; the work item will be idle when this completes.

Ok, good, that was my understanding ;-)

> Note that `stop()` can no longer be invoked from an ISR, though.

Yes, that's fine, both video stream start() and stop() should be (and are in current usages) executed in process context.

Regards,
Loic
